answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake into a shared kernel of escrow that only unlocks after verified work is completed; creating thousands of fake agents then costs real money per identity, since the stake is locked and slashed for fraud. The zenith of this design is reputation that compounds only through completed, paid tasks, so a fresh identity cannot fake history, while old credentials cannot be resold as a relic: they stay bound to the agent that earned them. Sybils become uneconomic.
